:::{#thm-frobenius-norm-columns}
#### The squared Frobenius norm adds up the squared column norms

If $\matr{A}$ is an $n \times p$ matrix
with columns $\vecf{a}_1, \ldots, \vecf{a}_p$, then

$$
\norm{\matr{A}}_F^2 = \sumjp \norm{\vecf{a}_j}^2.
$$

:::

::: proof

Entry $i$ of $\vecf{a}_j$ is $a_{ij}$, so

$$
\ba
\norm{\matr{A}}_F^2
&= \sumin \sumjp a_{ij}^2
&& \text{(@rem-frobenius-norm-entries)}
\\
&= \sumjp \sumin a_{ij}^2
&& \text{(swap the order of two finite sums)}
\\
&= \sumjp \norm{\vecf{a}_j}^2
&& \text{(@def-euclidean-norm, applied to each column)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-frobenius-norm-columns}
#### The Frobenius norm of a $2 \times 2$ matrix, column by column

The matrix $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$
in @exm-frobenius-norm has columns
$\vecf{a}_1 = (1, 3)$ and $\vecf{a}_2 = (2, 4)$, so

$$
\ba
\norm{\matr{A}}_F^2
&= \norm{\vecf{a}_1}^2 + \norm{\vecf{a}_2}^2
&& \text{(@thm-frobenius-norm-columns)}
\\
&= (1^2 + 3^2) + (2^2 + 4^2)
&& \text{(definition of the norm)}
\\
&= 10 + 20
&& \text{(square and add)}
\\
&= 30
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

which matches $\norm{\matr{A}}_F = \sqrt{30}$ from @exm-frobenius-norm.

:::
